blocks.passage:
A chart is not a story. A chart is raw material. The story is what you choose to say about it, and how you guide the audience through what matters.

Good data storytellers start with the message. They decide, before opening Excel, what they want the audience to conclude. Then they build the chart that supports that message in the cleanest, simplest way. Every colour, every axis label, every annotation serves the message or gets removed.

Numbers also need context to mean anything. "Sales grew 12 percent" sounds good until you discover the market grew 18 percent. Always provide the benchmark, the trend, or the comparison that makes the number interpretable. A number without context is noise dressed up as insight.

items.q: According to the text, what is a chart?
items.why: "A chart is not a story. A chart is raw material."

items.q: Where do good data storytellers start?
options: With the message — what they want the audience to conclude
items.why: "They decide, before opening Excel, what they want the audience to conclude."

items.q: What happens to a colour or label that doesn't serve the message?
items.why: "Every colour, every axis label, every annotation serves the message or gets removed."

items.q: Why is "Sales grew 12 percent" potentially misleading?
options: The market may have grown faster, e.g. 18 percent
items.why: "'Sales grew 12 percent' sounds good until you discover the market grew 18 percent."

items.q: "A number without context is noise dressed up as insight" means a number alone…
options: can look meaningful without actually being so
items.why: Inferência: sem referência ou comparação, o número parece insight mas não é.

audio.text:
I'm cutting the board update from five charts to one, because right now it's data without a story.

The message I want the board to walk away with is simple: our costs have fallen for three quarters in a row, and that trend is what's protecting our margin. Everything on the slide now serves that one message.

I've removed two charts entirely. One showed headcount, which is interesting but off-message. The other had so many colours you couldn't tell the trend from the noise. Gone.

On the chart that's left, I've added the benchmark. Our costs fell 9 percent, but on its own that number means nothing. So I've put the industry average next to it, which rose 2 percent. Now the board can see we didn't just improve — we improved while everyone else got more expensive.

And I've annotated the one outlier, that spike in Q2, so nobody wastes the meeting asking about it. One chart, one message, context included. Thirty seconds and they've got it.

items.q: Why is Harry cutting the update to one chart?
options: Because right now it's data without a story
items.why: "right now it's data without a story."

items.q: What is the single message Harry wants the board to take away?
options: Costs have fallen three quarters running, protecting the margin
items.why: "our costs have fallen for three quarters in a row, and that trend is what's protecting our margin."

items.q: Why did Harry remove the headcount chart?
items.why: "One showed headcount, which is interesting but off-message."

items.q: Why did Harry add the industry average to the chart?
options: To give context — the 9% fall means more when others rose 2%
items.why: "our costs fell 9 percent, but on its own that number means nothing. So I've put the industry average next to it."

items.q: Why did Harry annotate the Q2 outlier?
options: So nobody wastes the meeting asking about it
Because it was the main point
items.why: "I've annotated the one outlier… so nobody wastes the meeting asking about it."

items.q: "Costs **fell** three quarters in a row." To fall means…
items.why: To fall = cair, diminuir.

items.q: "Sales **remained stable** all year." To remain stable means…
items.why: Remain stable = permanecer estável.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Compare it against the industry **___** to see if it's good."
items.why: Benchmark = referência para comparação.

items.q: An **outlier** in data is…
options: a value far from the rest
items.why: Outlier = ponto fora da curva.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Revenue hit a **___** in December, the highest all year."
items.why: Peak = pico, o ponto mais alto.

items.q: "Costs have **gone up** sharply." To go up means to…
items.why: Go up = subir.

items.q: "Let the data **speak for itself**." If data speaks for itself, it…
options: needs no exaggeration to make the point
items.why: Speak for itself = ser claro por si só.

items.q: "Sales **picked up** in the second half." To pick up means to…
items.why: Pick up = melhorar, aumentar.

items.q: "Let's not **cherry-pick** the good numbers." To cherry-pick means to…
options: select only what supports your point
items.why: Cherry-pick = escolher a dedo só o que convém.

items.q: "That spike **stands out**." To stand out means to…
items.why: Stand out = destacar-se, saltar aos olhos.
